title: The price of hosting the Games
text: Hosting the Olympics {{1}} to guarantee prestige; today it tends to guarantee debt. Montreal, {{2}} needed three decades to pay off its 1976 stadium, became the cautionary tale, {{3}} the costs of security, transport and white-elephant venues have only grown since. In recent bidding rounds {{4}} a handful of cities have bothered to stand, and referendums in would-be host towns have repeatedly voted {{5}} playing host. The committee's response has been to beg candidates to use existing venues and temporary stands, {{6}} is an odd confession coming {{7}} an organisation that once demanded marble. The Games will survive — the spectacle is too useful to too many people — {{8}} the era in which a city felt lucky to be chosen is, like the great concrete stadiums, quietly crumbling.

gaps.explanation: 'Used to' — the past habit; the base verb follows.
Non-defining relative after the comma referring to the city.

gaps.hint: conjunction: cautionary tale, ___ the costs have grown
gaps.explanation: The two facts are simply added: and.
The focusing adverb stresses how few: only a handful.
'Vote against' — the referendums rejected the idea.
Sentential relative after the comma summing up the request.
'Coming from' — the source of the statement.

gaps.hint: conjunction: too useful, ___ the era is crumbling
gaps.explanation: Contrast between survival and decline: but.
